description: dryvist/.github master Renovate preset — the single source of truth for Renovate policy across ALL dryvist AND JacobPEvans repos. This is the MASTER: it extends no other repository’s config. JacobPEvans/.github extends THIS (github>dryvist/.github:renovate-presets), never the reverse. Consumers extend it via local>dryvist/.github (the default preset, which extends this) or directly via github>dryvist/.github:renovate-presets.

Architecture: this file holds global policy (auto-merge, trusted orgs, stability features, custom managers). Ecosystem grouping rules live in renovate-grouping.json and are pulled in via extends below. Inline description fields on each rule are the canonical documentation — keep them current.

WARNING: platformAutomerge MUST stay false. GitHub’s auto-merge queue has a known bug where PRs pass all checks but GitHub never executes the merge — PRs stall for days with no error. With false, Renovate merges directly via API with built-in retry logic. Do NOT set this to true.

customManagers.description: Renovate-annotated version pins in Nix files. HASH FIELDS ARE NOT UPDATED — only version strings. Each repo's fix-renovate-hashes.yml runs nix-update to fix adjacent hash = "sha256-..." fields after Renovate bumps a version. When adding a new fetchPypi/fetchurl package with a Renovate annotation, also add it to that repo's nix-update workflow and flake packages output.

description: Docker images pinned in Ansible role defaults as `<name>_image: "repo:tag"`. These live in plain YAML vars that no built-in Renovate manager scans, so image pins across ansible-proxmox-apps roles (prometheus_stack, netmon, qdrant_docker, ntfy_docker, mailpit_docker, unifi_metrics, seerr, ...) were untracked. Matched as the `docker` datasource so Renovate bumps the tag in place; image refs are self-describing (repo:tag) so no per-line `# renovate:` annotation is needed. Untagged refs (no colon) are not matched; local-only tags resolve to nothing and are skipped.

customManagers.description: Renovate-annotated version pins in Ansible role defaults (YAML). Mirrors the .nix annotation manager but for roles/**/defaults/main.yml — binary version vars (e.g. traefik_version, object_storage_rustfs_version) interpolated into download URLs that no built-in manager scans. Only lines carrying an explicit `# renovate:` annotation are matched. Release checksums are fetched at install time (no hash field to update here), so unlike the .nix manager no companion hash-fixer workflow is needed.

packageRules.description: Disable all updates in gh-aw generated files — managed by gh-aw-pin-refresh workflow, not Renovate

Major-version defaults, org-wide: 30-day grace period before a PR opens and never auto-merge (human review required). The grace gives upstream ecosystems time to surface breaking-change regressions before we adopt them. The own-orgs and trusted-orgs rules below are placed AFTER this rule so their values win per-attribute (Renovate merges packageRule attributes by last-match wins): own-orgs restores immediate auto-merge for JacobPEvans/** and dryvist/** majors, and trusted-orgs restores auto-merge (1-day grace) for the curated trusted-vendor list. Non-trusted-vendor majors match only this rule and stay held. CVE-driven bumps still bypass the grace via the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block (0 days).

Auto-merge own-org dependencies (JacobPEvans / JacobPEvans-personal + dryvist) — immediate, all ecosystems, all update types including major. Placed AFTER the major-default rule so we restore immediate auto-merge for our own majors that the major-default rule would otherwise hold for 30 days. JacobPEvans-personal is the renamed legacy personal account (dryvist/JacobPEvans account split); JacobPEvans/** still resolves via redirect but the current owner is listed explicitly.

dryvist/* first-party reusable workflows ride @main and must NEVER be digest-pinned (overrides the global pinGitHubActionDigests). They are self-owned; @main is the deliberate self-reference convention (SECURITY.md → Version Pinning). Without this, Renovate rewrites `uses: dryvist/...@main` to a SHA and auto-merges it (own-org rule above), silently breaking the convention across every consumer. Mirrors the zizmor `dryvist/*: ref-pin` allowance; CodeQL code scanning is managed as IaC in tofu-github, not here. Untrusted/external actions are unaffected — they keep SHA digests.

Auto-merge trusted orgs — all managers, all update types including MAJOR (1-day stabilization). Placed AFTER the major-default rule so this rule restores auto-merge for trusted-vendor majors that major-default would otherwise hold (Renovate merges packageRule attributes by last-match wins); non-trusted majors hit only major-default (30-day hold, no auto-merge). The `https://github.com/...` URL form of each entry was removed in this consolidation: `matchPackageNames` matches against the resolved `packageName`, which is `owner/repo` for both GitHub Actions and Nix flake `github:` inputs — the URL form never matched anything (verified via `gh search code 'depName=https://github.com/' org:JacobPEvans`, zero results).
Auto-merge trusted PyPI packages from HuggingFace (minor/patch only)
GitHub releases use v-prefixed tags for custom Nix packages
Twice-weekly schedule for all custom regex managers

Auto-merge Python minor/patch updates across every Python manager. Paired with the major-only `>=` bump rule below; the two share an identical manager list so behavior is symmetric: minor/patch auto-merge twice-weekly, major opens a PR (held by the 30-day major-default rule and reviewed manually). pip_setup/poetry/pipenv were added to match the bump rule's coverage — previously only pep621/pip_requirements auto-merged, an unintentional gap.

Bump Python `>=` lower bounds ONLY on major releases, and only to `>=N.0.0` form. The floor expresses the oldest acceptable major; minor/patch positions are reserved exclusively for CVE-mitigation pins. Minor/patch releases never trigger a floor bump — Renovate's default `replace` strategy already no-ops when the existing range satisfies the new version. Renovate's pep440 `bump` produces `>=N.M.P` natively; the companion normalizer workflow (follow-up issue in this repo) rewrites it to `>=N.0.0` after the PR opens. CVE EXCEPTION: when a known CVE is fixed only in a specific minor/patch release, pin the floor to the OLDEST secure version (e.g. `pyarrow 17.0.0 → PYSEC-2026-113 fixed in 23.0.1` → `pyarrow>=23.0.1`), NEVER the latest release. An inline comment block citing every CVE identifier the floor mitigates is REQUIRED above any floor that exceeds `>=N.0.0` form — see `mlx-benchmarks/space/requirements.txt` for the canonical pattern. The normalizer must preserve floors preceded by such a comment block. CVE-driven Renovate bumps themselves still use `bump` at all update types via the top-level `vulnerabilityAlerts` block, so security floor bumps remain immediate.
